PRICE PRIORS for recurring line types (statistical model fitted on the thresholds t revealed
in earlier games; gross amounts). How to use them:
- The amounts are final thresholds as they were revealed: they already contain whatever
  deductible, VAT and customary-price judgement applied in those cases, and they were computed
  from the full invoiced quantity (the whole quantity was indemnified there). For an
  indemnified line of this type take the stated amount for the line as t as it stands and give
  a price_log_sd that matches the stated range. Do not deduct a deductible from it and do not
  cut the invoiced quantity.
- Deviate only for something this case has and those cases did not: an aggregate cap or
  sub-limit that the lines of this invoice must share, a percentage reduction for a breached
  duty, or a purchase price or sum insured stated in the claim that limits the line.
- Whether a line is indemnified in THIS case is decided by the policy and the claim, not by
  the history. The history only says how often this line type was paid at all. A line type
  that was never indemnified before is usually an ancillary charge the policies do not carry;
  treat it as indemnified only if this policy clearly says so.
- line 5 "Vehicle costs": indemnified in 3 of 9 earlier cases, t = 0 in 6; when indemnified t per pc about 71 (80% range 54 to 95); revealed per pc: 12.9-16.1 (case 14*), >=60 (case 16*), >=68 (case 18) (* = other policy wording)

items.rationale: The on-site attendance and survey qualify under §7.1.7(e); the call-out is also the first attendance charge under §7.1.7(f). Estimate €135 gross without repeating the separately itemised pinpointing or technician work.
Pinpointing the supply-pipe leak is necessary source investigation under §7.1.7(e). Allow €185 gross for the specialist procedure, not for the contractor’s own equipment as a separate charge.

items.description: Kitchen floor and wall moisture measurement
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(e) covers measuring the extent of moisture in the affected floor and wall base. Allow €110 gross for one targeted survey.

Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(c) cover necessary labour at customary rates but not time already billed under the survey or pinpointing lines. Fourteen hours at €85 gross would be €1,190; for this localised job, I estimate four separately necessary hours, or €340.

Section 7.1.7(f) pays only the first travel, mileage or call-out charge on this contractor’s invoice; position 1 is the call-out. The conditional figure is €71 for one vehicle charge if it were found to be the first qualifying travel charge.
Local exposure of the leaking run is necessary repair work under §§7.1.1(b) and 7.1.5. Estimate €145 gross for access beneath the sink, without work on unaffected units.

items.description: Remove and dispose of damaged insulation
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(a) covers dismantling and disposal of affected materials. Allow two small insulation removals at €23 gross each, for €46 total.

items.description: Repair leak, replace copper section and reinsulate
items.rationale: Section 2.4.3(a) covers fracture of internal supply pipes, and §7.1.7(c) allows like-for-like materials and insulation. Allow €420 gross for a short standard copper repair with labour, excluding access and disposal billed separately.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) limit drying to areas with established loss-related moisture; the roof space was not affected. If substantiated, one small drying setup is estimated at €275 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and (e) cover necessary dryer hire for the affected kitchen. Allow €235 gross for one unit over an ordinary drying cycle, without a separate electricity allowance under §7.1.8(d).

items.description: Dry kitchen floor and wall base
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers necessary drying of the affected floor and wall base. Allow €390 gross for setup, monitoring and completion work, excluding the dryer hire already billed at position 10 under §7.1.8(c).

items.description: Transition pieces and insulation for repaired pipe
items.rationale: The plumbing repair at position 8 already bills reinstatement of the pipe section and its standard insulation. Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) bar duplicate or unsupported costs; if separately necessary materials were documented, estimate €85 gross.

Section 7.1.8(a) excludes general cleaning even within the work area, but §5.2.1 can cover removal of identifiable repair debris. If this charge is substantiated as debris removal rather than routine cleanup, allow €55 gross.
Section 7.1.7(f) covers the first travel charge on this contractor’s invoice for covered work. Apply the €71 gross prior for one vehicle charge.
Section 7.1.7(h) covers taking the damaged furnishing out of the dwelling. Allow €35 gross for carrying out one plain pine table, separate from haulage.

items.description: Transport and dispose of damaged table
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(h) and 5.2.1 cover haulage and disposal of the damaged furnishing. Allow €45 for haulage plus €25 for disposal, or €70 gross for the line.
The scheduled new-for-old option under §§4.4 and 7.1.1(d) removes depreciation. The same model costs €440 × 1.19 = €523.60 gross, including VAT if incurred under §7.7.
Section 7.1.7(h) expressly covers delivery of the replacement furnishing. Allow €50 gross for one local delivery, without duplicating the separately billed vehicle charge.

items.description: Assemble table and clean its placement area
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(h) covers setting up the replacement and cleaning the spot where the damaged item stood. Allow €55 gross for simple assembly plus €15 for local cleaning, or €70 total.

Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first contractor travel charge; this is the first vehicle charge on the carpentry invoice. Apply the €71 gross prior, treating table delivery as a distinct service under §7.1.7(h).

Section 7.1.7(f) excludes the second travel charge on the same invoice regardless of the number of visits. The conditional €71 is the ordinary single-trip benchmark, not an allowance for this return visit.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(f) exclude inspection of items not established as affected, and §4.2.6 defines covered furnishings as kept inside the dwelling. If a covered inspection were substantiated, estimate €65 gross.
